# grafana-agento11y-hermes: agent install guide

You are an LLM agent (likely Hermes itself) helping a user install and configure
this plugin. Follow the steps below in order. Ask the user for any value you
do not have. Do **not** guess endpoints, regions, or tokens.

Repo: https://github.com/alexander-akhmetov/grafana-agento11y-hermes
Plugin name (in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`): `agento11y`
Hermes upstream: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent

## What this plugin does

Records every Hermes LLM call and tool invocation to **Grafana Cloud Agent
Observability** (agento11y in package names and env vars). It has two
independent channels. You can configure either, both, or neither:

| Channel | What flows | Where it shows up |
|---|---|---|
| **Generations** | Per-LLM-call records with prompts/responses/tool calls | Observability -> AI -> Conversations |
| **OTel traces + metrics** | `gen_ai.client.*` spans and metrics | Grafana Cloud Traces / Metrics data sources |

The two channels use two different endpoints but **share a single
Grafana Cloud token**. The setup page in the Agent Observability app
creates that token and prints every env var both channels need, so you do
not assemble anything by hand (Step 3).

### What conversation data leaves the machine (read this to the user)

By default this plugin sends **full conversation content** to Grafana Cloud:

- Every user prompt and every assistant response (text content).
- Every tool call's **arguments** and the tool's **result** (truncated per
  string at `AGENTO11Y_HERMES_MAX_CHARS`, default 12000 chars).
- Conversation history snapshots that get attached to each generation as
  `input` so the UI can show the full turn.
- Token usage, model name, finish reason, and timing.

Tool args and results in particular can include filesystem paths, command
output, file contents, API responses, and anything else Hermes tools
produce. Treat the destination Grafana Cloud stack as a place this content
will live.

This is a deliberate choice. The SDK's own default is `no_tool_content`,
but the plugin sets `full` because tool args/results are usually the most
useful thing to see in the AI Observability UI.

The privacy lever is **`AGENTO11Y_CONTENT_CAPTURE_MODE=metadata_only`**. Set
it before starting Hermes and the plugin still records every call, but
only counts, model name, usage, finish reason, and timing leave the
machine. No prompts, no responses, no tool args, no tool results. Both
channels honor it.

```bash
# The setting to use when content must not leave the machine: only counts,
# model name, usage, timing. No prompts, responses, or tool I/O:
export AGENTO11Y_CONTENT_CAPTURE_MODE=metadata_only

# Sample only a fraction of calls (defense-in-depth, not redaction):
export AGENTO11Y_HERMES_SAMPLE_RATE=0.1   # 10%
```

The plugin does **no PII redaction**. It bounds payload structure
(depth, entries, per-string length) but does not pattern-match for
secrets, emails, or keys. If the user has compliance constraints, set
`AGENTO11Y_CONTENT_CAPTURE_MODE=metadata_only`, or route through a Grafana
Alloy / OTel Collector that does redaction before forwarding.

## Step 1: Install into the same environment as `hermes`

```bash
which hermes                     # find the python that runs hermes
<that-python> -m pip install grafana-agento11y-hermes
```

If `hermes` lives in a venv or pipx env, install into *that* env, not the
system Python. The plugin loads as an entry point. If it is in the wrong
env, Hermes will not see it.

## Step 2: Enable in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`

`hermes plugins enable agento11y` does not currently see pip-installed plugins.
Edit the YAML directly:

```yaml
plugins:
  enabled:
    - agento11y
```

If the file or `plugins:` block does not exist, create it. Preserve any
existing entries.

## Step 3: Get the credentials from the setup page

Every value comes from one page. Ask the user to open it in their stack:

**`https://<stack>.grafana.net/a/grafana-agento11y-app/setup`**

`<stack>` is their Grafana Cloud stack slug. If the user does not have a
stack yet, they can create one for free at
https://grafana.com/auth/sign-up/create-user/. The free tier is enough
to run this plugin.

Tell the user to do two things on that page, in this order:

1. On the **API token** row, click **Create token**. One token covers
   both channels. Grafana shows it once.
2. Click **Copy as environment variables** at the bottom of the
   credentials panel, and paste the block to you.

Order matters. Copied before the token exists, the block carries
`AGENTO11Y_AUTH_TOKEN=<create a token above>` and an unencoded OTLP auth
header.

The block looks like this:

```
AGENTO11Y_ENDPOINT=https://agento11y-<...>.grafana.net
AGENTO11Y_PROTOCOL=http
AGENTO11Y_AUTH_MODE=basic
AGENTO11Y_AUTH_TENANT_ID=123456
AGENTO11Y_AUTH_TOKEN=glc_...
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://otlp-gateway-<...>.grafana.net/otlp
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS='Authorization=Basic <base64 of "123456:glc_...">'
```

Check the pasted block before you use it:

- Any value still in angle brackets is a placeholder, not a credential.
  Do not export it. Send the user back to the setup page.
- The first five lines are the generations channel, the last two are the
  OTel channel. Each group works without the other.

The token is a live secret. Keep it in what the user pastes and in what
you write to their env; do not echo it back in summaries, and do not
write it into a file the user did not name.

## Step 4: Set the env vars

The values have to be in Hermes's process environment when it starts.
**Ask the user how they want to set them.** Some people put env vars in a
shell profile, others in a project `.envrc`, others pull from a secret
manager, others prefix `KEY=value hermes …` inline. Don't edit anything on
their behalf without confirmation.

The pasted block has no `export` keywords, so a shell profile or `.envrc`
needs `export ` in front of each line.

If the user keeps credentials in `~/.hermes/.env`, tell them hermes loads
that file with override on (`hermes_cli/env_loader.py`), so a value there
beats the same variable exported in the shell, with no warning. A stale
token in that file is a silent failure.

### Optional knobs (do not set unless the user asks)

| Variable | Default | When to change |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENTO11Y_AGENT_NAME` | `hermes` | Multiple Hermes deployments and you want to distinguish them in the UI |
| `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` | `hermes` | Same reason |
| `AGENTO11Y_CONTENT_CAPTURE_MODE` | `full` | Set `metadata_only` to keep recording every call while no prompts, responses or tool I/O leave the machine |
| `AGENTO11Y_DEBUG` | `false` | Set `true` for verbose SDK logs while debugging install |
| `AGENTO11Y_HERMES_SAMPLE_RATE` | `1.0` | Lower if volume is high. Range `0.0`–`1.0` |
| `AGENTO11Y_HERMES_MAX_CHARS` | `12000` | Truncation cap per redacted string |
| `AGENTO11Y_HERMES_OTEL_AUTO` | `true` | Set `false` if the host app already installs `TracerProvider` / `MeterProvider` |

## Step 5: Verify

Run interactive hermes. One-shot mode (`hermes -z`) calls
`logging.disable()` for the whole run (`hermes_cli/oneshot.py`), so no
plugin log line reaches any file and the check below cannot tell you
whether the install works.

```bash
AGENTO11Y_DEBUG=true hermes
```

Tail `~/.hermes/logs/agent.log`. On a clean install you should see:

```
grafana-agento11y-hermes: installed TracerProvider with OTLP HTTP exporter
grafana-agento11y-hermes: installed MeterProvider with OTLP HTTP exporter
grafana-agento11y-hermes: client initialized (generations=configured, otel=configured)
```

If a channel is unconfigured the corresponding line says `unconfigured`
instead of `configured`. That is fine if the user opted out of that channel.

Have the user ask Hermes any question, then open **Grafana Cloud -> Observability -> AI -> Conversations**. The generation should
appear within a few seconds. Check **Traces** (filter for
`service.name = hermes`) for the OTel side.

## Common failure modes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin lines never appear in `agent.log` | Installed into wrong Python env | Run `which hermes`, install into that env |
| Plugin lines never appear in `agent.log`, but generations do arrive | Checked with `hermes -z`, which disables logging for the run | Check with interactive `hermes` |
| Credentials look right but the plugin reads old ones | `~/.hermes/.env` overrides the shell environment | Update or remove the stale entry in `~/.hermes/.env` |
| `hermes plugins list` does not show `agento11y` | Hermes does not list pip-installed plugins | Expected. Confirm from `plugins.enabled` in `config.yaml` and from data arriving |
| Plugin loads but `generations=not_configured` | `AGENTO11Y_AUTH_TOKEN` empty or `AGENTO11Y_AUTH_MODE=none` | Re-export and reload shell |
| `401 Unauthorized` on generations | The token line is still a placeholder, or the token cannot write generations | Create the token on the setup page and copy the block again |
| `401` on OTLP traces/metrics | The token cannot write traces and metrics, or the header was not copied from the setup page | Create the token on the setup page and copy the block again |
| `404` on generations | `AGENTO11Y_ENDPOINT` was hand-constructed with wrong region | Copy it from the setup page instead |
| Traces/metrics silently absent | Host app installed its own provider, or `AGENTO11Y_HERMES_OTEL_AUTO=false` | Either let the plugin install providers, or have the host app add OTLP exporters |

## Hard invariants for the agent

- **Take the values from the setup page, do not build them.** Never invent
  an endpoint from a region string. Regions are not always literal
  (`prod-us`, `prod-eu`, `prod-ap-southeast-1`, and so on) and the URLs
  sometimes include extra segments. The same holds for the base64 in the
  OTLP header.
- **Never export a placeholder.** Anything in angle brackets
  (`<create a token above>`, `<endpoint from the OpenTelemetry setup
  link>`, `<base64 of "…">`) means the user skipped a step on the setup
  page. Stop and ask. The plugin fails open silently, so the user will
  not learn from Hermes that the value was wrong.
- **One token covers both channels.** The setup page's token works as
  `AGENTO11Y_AUTH_TOKEN` *and* as the password half of the OTel basic-auth
  header. Do not send the user to "Generate now" on the Cloud portal's
  OpenTelemetry card. They end up with two tokens to rotate for no benefit.
- **Never overwrite existing env vars without confirming.** If the user
  already has `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` set for another collector,
  ask before changing it. The plugin will respect whatever provider the
  host installs if `AGENTO11Y_HERMES_OTEL_AUTO=false`.
- **Handle the token as a secret.** It grants write access to the user's
  Grafana Cloud stack. Put it only where the user says to put it, and do
  not repeat it in your own output.
